fields.meta_title: Compatibility Quiz: Score How Two People Match | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Play the compatibility quiz on this page, or build one that two people answer apart, scored by matching answers. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Compatibility Quiz That Scores How Two People Match
fields.hero_description: Build a compatibility quiz two people answer apart, with a match score per pair, or play the eight-question quiz below.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Compatibility Quiz
fields.features_subheading: One prompt sets the questions, the pair links, and the scoring. A follow-up prompt changes any of it before the next round.
fields.feature_1:
Questions about an ordinary week

Describe who the quiz pairs, and Emergent drafts questions about how people actually spend their time, such as weeknights, guests, and noise. Edit any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Two links that join as one pair

Each person answers from their own link, on their own schedule. The quiz joins the two sets of answers under one pair, and neither person ever sees the other's picks.
fields.feature_3:
A match score for every pair

When both halves of a pair are in, the app counts every question they answered the same and saves the score, such as 11 of 12, beside the two responses in your table.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when both people finish

No one has to watch for the second response. The app sends an email or Slack alert the moment a pair completes, with both names and the match score in the message body.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer in a database you own

Every response lands as a row in a database you own, tagged with its pair. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so a full incoming class can answer inside the same week.
fields.feature_6:
Full code export on paid plans

Own the whole build. On paid plans, export the quiz's full code to your GitHub repository, and rerun next season's pairing round without rebuilding a single question.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Groups That Pair People by Match Score
fields.tab_content_1:
Mirela and Leah land in Room 214 together

Every June, Wrenford State University's housing office sends its incoming students a 12-question compatibility quiz, and 412 answered this year. The app scores every two-student pair, and Mirela Vosberg and Leah Amadife match on 11 of 12 answers, the closest pair in the pool. They get Room 214 of Arden Hall.
fields.tab_content_2:
Davor meets Pippin after a 7 of 8 match

Davor Jansek filled out Thistle Creek Animal Rescue's quiz: 8 questions on yard time, other pets, and hours away from home. Staff answered the same 8 for every dog. Pippin tops Davor's list at 7 of 8, ahead of Clover at 6 of 8, and counselor Sabine Dillane gets the ranked list before his Saturday visit.
fields.tab_content_3:
16 pairs clear the bar and 2 reach Alan

Harlow Pines Chamber of Commerce pairs 18 mentees with mentors by score. Both sides answer the same 10 questions about meeting cadence, feedback style, and goals, and the build routes any pair under 6 of 10 to program director Alan Brooks. This round, 16 pairs stand and 2 land on his desk.
fields.tab_content_4:
A taproom screen ranks 31 couples by match

On the second Thursday of February, Saltbox Brewing runs a couples night. Each of the 31 couples answers 10 questions apart on their phones, and the screen above the bar reranks the room as scores land. Nate and Kira Hatcher finish first at 10 of 10, and every pair's picks sit in the brewery's table before close.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Compatibility Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a compatibility quiz that scores two sets of answers fairly, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the match rule in numbers
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide first whether the two people know each other. A couple answers about themselves and compares. Strangers, like roommates or mentor pairs, need both sides to answer the same profile questions so the scores mean the same thing for everyone.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about what people do, not what they think of each other. How many nights a week someone cooks at home compares cleanly between two sets of answers. Whether someone calls themselves easygoing does not, because everyone does.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Scoring compares picks: both people must see the same questions with the same fixed options, in the same order. Skip free-text fields for anything scored, because two honest answers written in different words never count as a match.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick how a pair is scored: count the questions both answered the same, out of the total. Then set the threshold that matters, such as 6 of 10 to confirm a pairing, and write down what happens to any pair below it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Keep the two answer sets apart
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give each person their own link and hold scoring until both finish. Neither side should see the other's picks while answering, or the second person matches the first instead of answering honestly, and the score stops meaning anything.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run the quiz with two real pairs: one you expect to score high and one you expect to score low. If the two scores come out close together, the questions are too easy to agree on. Replace the ones every pair answers the same.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Choose what each person sees when scoring ends: usually the match score alone, never the other person's answers unless both agreed to that up front. The organizer keeps the full table, and the score is what gets shared or shown on a screen.

faq_plan.a: A compatibility quiz asks two people the same questions and counts how many answers match. The count becomes the pair's score. Beyond couples, the same format pairs roommates with roommates and mentors with mentees, anywhere a match between two sets of answers has to be put in numbers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a compatibility quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the quiz in one prompt: the questions, how the two people answer, and what the match score decides. Emergent's AI survey builder turns that prompt into the quiz, two links per pair, and the table every answer lands in. Test it with two real pairs, then publish and share the links.

faq_plan.q: What are good compatibility quiz questions?
faq_plan.a: Good compatibility quiz questions cover habits a week actually shows: bedtimes, guests, cleaning, and time alone. Give each one 3 or 4 fixed options. A question works when two people who live well together would pick the same option for the same reason.

faq_plan.q: Can a compatibility quiz collect emails before showing the result?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for an email on the last screen, before the score, and the quiz doubles as a quiz funnel: the result goes out by email, and the list keeps every pair who played. At a public event, that list is who gets the invite next time.

faq_plan.q: How is a compatibility quiz scored between two people?
faq_plan.a: Count the questions both people answered identically and report it out of the total, such as 7 of 8. Exact-match counting is easy to explain on a screen. Weighted scoring, where some questions count double, fits when one topic matters more. Describe either rule in the prompt and Emergent builds the scoring.

faq_plan.q: Do both people see each other's answers in a compatibility quiz?
faq_plan.a: Only if you build it that way, and the safer default is no. Show each person the match score and keep individual picks private; a roommate quiz that leaks answers invites conflict before move-in. With Emergent, every answer stays in a database you own, and you decide exactly who sees it.

faq_plan.q: Can a compatibility quiz match one person against several profiles?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Score one person's answers against each stored profile and rank the results, the way a shelter ranks its dogs for an adopter. A dog breed quiz works on the same logic, mapping one set of answers to the closest result. Showing the top 2 or 3 matches gives the person a real choice instead of a verdict.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a compatibility quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Keep a compatibility quiz between 8 and 12 questions. Under 8, one matched answer moves the score too much. Past 12, you risk one half of a pair never finishing, and an incomplete pair cannot be scored. The quiz on this page asks 8.

faq_plan.q: Can one compatibility quiz pair a whole group at once?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Everyone answers the same questions once, the app scores every possible pair, and the highest matches are paired first. A dorm intake and an 18-mentee mentoring round run the same build at different sizes. Decide up front who resolves the leftovers when the group is odd.

faq_plan.q: Does a live compatibility quiz work for an event night?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Couples answer on their phones, a shared screen reorders the pairs as scores arrive, and the room watches positions change. The leaderboard build also powers a marketing quiz, where the same scoring ranks customers instead of couples; the venue leaves the night with a list.

quiz.title: Compatibility Quiz: What Should a Good Match Share With You?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how you actually spend a week. Your result names what a compatible roommate, partner, or travel companion most needs to share with you.

questions.text: It is 9 pm on a Tuesday. Where are you?

options.text: In bed or close to it, same as most Tuesdays
Out, because something came up and I said yes
Home with headphones on, deep in my own thing
Cooking for whoever happened to come over

questions.text: A free Saturday appears. What happens to it?

options.text: The usual: errands in the morning, slow afternoon
A day trip I invent by 10 am
A solo project I have been saving up
A long lunch that keeps growing as people text

questions.text: How do you feel about houseguests?

options.text: Fine with notice, a day or two ahead
The more spontaneous the visit, the better
Short visits, and my room stays off the tour
The guest room is basically always made up

questions.text: What does your ideal shared dinner look like?

options.text: Same night every week, same table
A new place I have been meaning to try
Takeout, two screens, low conversation
Six people, two more arriving late

questions.text: A trip is coming up. What is your role?

options.text: I book things early and keep the confirmations
I leave room in the plan for surprises
I plan my own mornings and meet the group at lunch
I am the one who invited everyone else

questions.text: How should a quiet evening at home go?

options.text: Lights low by 10, phones away
Quiet is fine until a better offer texts
Both home, separate rooms, perfectly happy
Quiet means only three friends came over

questions.text: What is your rule for weeknight noise?

options.text: Low after 9, and everyone knows it
Noise is fine; silence is what unsettles me
Headphones solve most of it for me
A loud kitchen is the sound of a good week

questions.text: How do you recharge after a long week?

options.text: The same ritual every Friday night
A change of scenery, decided that day
A full day with no plans and no talking
People over, music on, kitchen busy

results.title: A Shared Routine
results.description: Your answers lean toward set bedtimes, quiet evenings, and a week that runs on rhythm. A good match for you keeps roughly your hours and treats the calendar as a promise. Agree on wake-up times and weeknight noise early, and the rest follows.

results.title: New Plans Energy
results.description: Your answers lean toward saying yes first and planning later. A good match for you brings ideas of their own and does not need a reason to leave the house. Ask a potential roommate or travel companion about their last unplanned weekend, and listen closely.

results.title: Side by Side
results.description: Your answers lean toward company without commentary: two people in one room, each deep in their own project. A good match for you respects closed doors and quiet hours without taking either personally. Make alone time an explicit part of any shared plan.

results.title: A Full Table
results.description: Your answers lean toward group dinners, open invitations, and a home people drop into. A good match for you says yes to hosting and does not count the chairs. Check early how many guests feel normal to each of you, and compare notes before sharing a lease.

plan.angle: The top 10 is quiz-taker pages for couples: relationship tests from therapist sites, a BuzzFeed love test, wikiHow and Reddit threads, and none of them shows how two sets of answers become a match. This page lets a visitor play an eight-question compatibility quiz on how two people spend their time, then shows four builds that compare answers between people: a university pairing roommates, an animal rescue matching an adopter to dogs, a chamber of commerce pairing mentors with mentees, and a brewery's couples night with a match leaderboard. The FAQ covers question choice, scoring, privacy between the two people, group pairing, and quiz length, so it serves a builder rather than a quiz-taker.
